en: Oil floats on water because it is less dense, so pouring water on a grease fire will only spread the burning oil.
Water expands when it freezes into solid ice, so leaving a sealed glass bottle in the freezer can cause it to shatter.
Mixing liquid bleach and vinegar causes a dangerous chemical reaction that releases toxic chlorine gas, so these cleaners must never be combined.
Dissolving oral rehydration salts in clean water forms a homogeneous solution that quickly replaces lost fluids and electrolytes during severe diarrhea.
Metals are excellent thermal conductors, so cooking pots use wooden or plastic handles to prevent heat from transferring to your hands.
Squeezing lemon juice on sliced apples prevents browning because the citric acid slows down the chemical oxidation reaction with oxygen in the air.
Rubber is an electrical insulator that blocks the flow of current, which is why electricians wear thick rubber gloves to avoid shocks.
Breathing helium from a balloon displaces oxygen in your lungs, so inhaling too much of this lighter gas can cause dangerous fainting.
Iron reacts with oxygen and moisture to form flaky rust through a chemical change, which can weaken metal roofs during strong typhoons.
Pouring muddy water through a clean cotton cloth acts as a physical filter to trap large solid particles before boiling the water for drinking.
Heating an aerosol spray can increases the kinetic energy of the gas inside, which can cause the metal container to dangerously explode.
Shaking a bottle of liquid antibiotic mixes the settled solid medicine particles back into the liquid suspension to ensure you get the correct dose.
